content.user_title: Design Controlled Email Workflows for AI Agents
content.value_statement: Agent email workflows need isolated identities, reliable replies, and clear sending permissions. This skill guides Cooper Email architecture with owner approval, delivery controls, and explicit trust boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Explains persistent agent inboxes, temporary inbox expiration, workspace isolation, and inbox-scoped keys.
Outlines reply loops with bounded waiting, extracted message text, parent message identifiers, and read-state updates.
Describes owner-approved sends, draft reapproval, owner status updates, and authenticated email tasks.
Explains verification-code retrieval using request-time filters, service filters, deadlines, and retry limits.
Compares signed webhooks, long-polling, and event listing for incoming email.
Documents idempotent sends, suppression handling, recipient allow lists, and defenses against injection, spoofing, and key exposure.
limitations: Provides architecture guidance, not executable integration code or individual action implementations.
Requires separately available Cooper Email tools and credentials to perform email operations.
Does not implement application state storage, webhook hosting, or secret management.
Inbound screening remains heuristic and does not guarantee protection from malicious email.

use_cases.title: Plan a dedicated agent inbox
use_cases.description: Choose persistent or temporary inboxes and define reply handling without granting access to a personal mailbox.

use_cases.title: Define approval for sensitive messages
use_cases.description: Design verified-owner approval and recipient restrictions for financial, legal, or first-contact email workflows.

use_cases.title: Review email integration boundaries
use_cases.description: Assess webhook authentication, owner task verification, credential scope, and treatment of untrusted email content.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an inbox model
prompt_templates.prompt: My agent performs [task]. Compare a persistent inbox with temporary inboxes per run. Recommend an identity, expiration, and key-scope strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reply loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cooper Email reply loop for [workflow] without a public endpoint. Include deadlines, extracted text, threading, read-state updates, and external job state.

prompt_templates.title: Add owner approval
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan owner-approved email for [sensitive workflow]. Include verified ownership, draft reapproval after edits, recipient allow lists, owner updates, and duplicate-send prevention.

prompt_templates.title: Review an event-driven architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Cooper Email architecture: [design]. Assess webhook signatures, timestamp freshness, owner verification, injection boundaries, secret storage, suppressions, and retries. Propose changes without sending mail.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess security and reliability together.

output_examples.input: Plan a persistent inbox for a support agent without a public webhook endpoint.
output: Create a dedicated inbox with a stable client identifier and an inbox-scoped key.
Use long-polling with a job deadline and read extracted message text.
Reply using the parent message identifier, then mark handled mail read.
Keep job state outside email and treat all incoming content as untrusted.

output_examples.input: Plan email controls for an agent that sends financial notices.
output: Establish a verified owner and enable approval mode before sending.
Require reapproval whenever recipients, subject, body, or attachments change.
Restrict recipients with an allow list and use idempotency for every send.
Respect suppressions and review bounce and complaint metrics.

best_practices: Use separate inboxes for independent agents and prefer narrowly scoped keys.
Enable owner approval for sensitive sends and verify owner tasks before treating replies as instructions.
Combine bounded waits and idempotent sends with signature verification for webhook-based workflows.
anti_patterns: Granting an agent broad access to a personal mailbox when a dedicated inbox is sufficient.
Treating email subjects, bodies, attachments, or links as trusted instructions.
Retrying sends without idempotency or ignoring recipient suppressions.

faq.question: Does this skill send or receive email by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance. Actual operations require Cooper Email tools, credentials, and the relevant action workflows.

faq.question: When should an agent use a temporary inbox?
faq.answer: Use temporary inboxes for isolated jobs, sign-ups, or trials. Set expiration deliberately; deletion follows the service cleanup schedule.

faq.question: Do incoming replies require a public webhook endpoint?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes long-polling and event listing as alternatives. Webhook deployments require signature verification and rejection of stale timestamps.

faq.question: How does owner approval affect edited drafts?
faq.answer: Approval mode holds outgoing mail for the verified owner. Changing recipients, subject, body, or attachments requires approval again.

faq.question: Can an agent trust the sender address as proof of ownership?
faq.answer: No. The guidance requires an authenticated owner task with the verified_owner flag. Screening labels alone are not a guarantee.

faq.question: How should API keys be stored?
faq.answer: Use a secret store or environment variable. Never place keys in chat, logs, commits, or email, and prefer inbox-scoped keys.
